Why is EverCommerce stock up today?

No company news, analyst action or filing explained the move. Stocks rallied on Black Friday as AI fears faded, according to Barron's, and the Russell 2000 small-cap index rose 0.8%. EverCommerce rose far more than the market, while software peers Shopify (up 4.7%) and Salesforce (up 0.2%) moved by much less.

How unusual is this move for EverCommerce?

A move of this size is unusual for EverCommerce, and the stock last moved this much on Nov. 25, when it rose 12.1%. It fell 18.8% on Nov. 24 and 13.3% on Nov. 10, and no cause was identified for either drop. It has had 5 unusual jumps in the past 12 months; the biggest recent one, 19.8% on Sept. 14, came after it raised its share buyback plan by $25M to a total of $325M.

Shares have started to rebound. They rose 2.04% in the last session before Thanksgiving and 9.2% over three sessions from $180.62.

detail:
Why Is Salesforce Stock Rising Today?
Fiona Craig

CRM
^IXIC
Trade CRM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Technology ©Adobe Stock Images

Salesforce shares rose 1.6% in pre-market trading on Friday, recovering above the $200 level as US equity futures advanced and investors returned to enterprise software stocks following Wednesday's technology sector sell-off.

The rebound comes ahead of Salesforce's third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings announcement, with investors monitoring the company's financial performance and adoption of its artificial intelligence products.

What Is Driving Salesforce's Share Price Recovery?

Salesforce's gains coincided with a broader recovery across US technology stocks following Wednesday's volatile trading session, during which the Nasdaq briefly declined nearly 5%.

Renewed buying interest in established enterprise software companies followed substantial selling pressure across AI semiconductor stocks.

Salesforce shares have fallen approximately 27% from their September peak and remain considerably below their 52-week high of $269.11.

What Are Analysts Expecting From Salesforce's Upcoming Earnings Report?

Salesforce is scheduled to publish its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results after the market closes on 2 December.

Analysts expect earnings per share of $3.45 on revenue of approximately $11.46 billion.

Options market pricing indicates an anticipated share price movement of around 11% surrounding the earnings announcement, reflecting expectations of significant volatility.

Investors will be monitoring adoption of Salesforce's Agentforce platform and the company's progress in integrating artificial intelligence across its enterprise software business.

What Is Wall Street's Current View on Salesforce?

Erste Group recently downgraded Salesforce from Buy to Hold, introducing a more cautious assessment ahead of the upcoming quarterly results.

However, analyst recommendations remain predominantly positive, with 40 Buy ratings, 14 Hold ratings and one Sell rating.

The forthcoming earnings announcement will provide investors with updated information on the company's financial performance and AI strategy.

How Is the Broader Market Supporting Salesforce Shares?

US equity futures recorded substantial gains ahead of Friday's shortened Black Friday trading session, with Nasdaq 100 futures rising nearly 3% and S&P 500 futures advancing approximately 2%.

No major economic data releases are scheduled for Friday, following Thursday's Thanksgiving market closure.

The recovery follows significant losses across US equities during November, driven partly by concerns surrounding AI regulation and expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December.

Salesforce's pre-market advance reflects improving technology sector sentiment and investor positioning ahead of its quarterly earnings announcement, although the stock remains substantially below its recent highs.

Factors Likely to Influence Salesforce's Q3 Results

Salesforce appears well-positioned to deliver another quarter of revenue growth, driven by increasing demand for its cloud-based software and AI-powered solutions. The company's focus on helping businesses improve productivity through AI agents is likely to have supported customer spending during the quarter. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Salesforce reported revenues of $11.35 billion, up 11% year over year. Subscription and support revenues increased 12% to $10.8 billion, highlighting continued demand for its core offerings.

The growing adoption of Agentforce and Data 360 is likely to have been a major growth driver. In the second quarter, combined Agentforce and Data 360 annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached nearly $3.9 billion, increasing more than 210% year over year. Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than 240%. Meanwhile, customers generated 3.2 billion Agentic Work Units in the quarter, up 97% sequentially. Rising adoption of AI agents and growing customer engagement could have supported Salesforce's subscription revenues in the to-be-reported quarter.

title: Should AI Pricing Change Require Action From Salesforce Stock Investors?

Salesforce has changed pricing for its AI Help Agent, moving from per seat licenses to charging customers for each successful AI answer delivered.

This shift puts more of Salesforce's revenue opportunity on actual AI usage, tying cash generation directly to how often enterprises lean on automation.

The focus now turns to how Salesforce's usage based AI pricing could affect the broader investment narrative and its long term cash engine.

Spot opportunities beyond Salesforce by scanning hand picked AI productivity plays in our 45 profitable AI stocks that aren't just burning cash that are already monetising automation rather than just talking about it.

Salesforce Investment Narrative Recap

To be a shareholder in Salesforce, you need to believe the business can shift from selling seats to selling AI driven activity without losing economic power. The move to usage based pricing for Help Agent leans straight into that view. It ties revenue more tightly to how much automation customers actually use, which may sharpen both upside and downside swings in the near term.

Right now the key short term catalyst is execution around Agentforce and AI consumption heading into the December 2 earnings print. The biggest risk is still that AI reduces human seats faster than usage based Agentforce and Data 360 revenue scale. If this pricing change does not materially lift adoption or usage, the immediate impact on that risk appears limited.

The most relevant recent data point is the forecast that Subscription and support revenue from Agentforce Apps could reach US$7.33b, with a very large year on year percentage change. That figure gives you a rough sense of how central Agentforce has become to the Salesforce story and why the Help Agent pricing reset matters operationally.

michaelyang, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, argues that the key question is whether consumption based AI and data can offset any pressure on seat based licences. From that perspective, the upcoming earnings call, usage metrics and any commentary on Help Agent adoption sit at the center of both the main catalyst and the core execution risk.

The Salesforce narrative from michaelyang anchors its fair value at US$255.90, based on revenue rising 8.9% a year and a future profit margin of 19.0%. Together, these support a forecast of durable cash generation under a more usage focused AI model.

title: Wall Street's Insights Into Key Metrics Ahead of Salesforce (CRM) Q3 Earnings

Wall Street's Insights Into Key Metrics Ahead of Salesforce (CRM) Q3 Earnings
Zacks Equity Research

Trading disclosure

The upcoming report from Salesforce (CRM) is expected to reveal quarterly earnings of $3.43 per share, indicating an increase of 5.5% compared to the year-ago period. Analysts forecast revenues of $11.46 billion, representing an increase of 11.7% year over year.

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days. This represents how the covering analysts, as a whole, have reassessed their initial estimates during this timeframe.

Before a company reveals its earnings, it is vital to take into account any changes in earnings projections. These revisions play a pivotal role in predicting the possible reactions of investors toward the stock. Multiple empirical studies have consistently shown a strong association between trends in earnings estimates and the short-term price movements of a stock.

While investors usually depend on consensus earnings and revenue estimates to assess the business performance for the quarter, delving into analysts' forecasts for certain key metrics often provides a more comprehensive understanding.

In light of this perspective, let's dive into the average estimates of certain Salesforce metrics that are commonly tracked and forecasted by Wall Street analysts.

Analysts' assessment points toward 'Revenues- Professional services and other' reaching $515.70 million. The estimate suggests a change of -3.3% year over year.

The average prediction of analysts places 'Revenues- Subscription and support' at $10.95 billion. The estimate indicates a change of +12.6% from the prior-year quarter.

Analysts predict that the 'Revenues- Subscription and support- Agentforce Apps' will reach $7.33 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +219.2%.

The combined assessment of analysts suggests that 'Revenues- Subscription and support- Data 360, Headless Platform, & Other' will likely reach $3.61 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +65.7%.

The collective assessment of analysts points to an estimated 'Geographic Revenue- Americas' of $8.00 billion. The estimate points to a change of +19.3% from the year-ago quarter.

According to the collective judgment of analysts, 'Geographic Revenue- Asia Pacific' should come in at $1.13 billion. The estimate suggests a change of +4.2% year over year.

Analysts forecast 'Geographic Revenue- Europe' to reach $2.35 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of -5%.

The consensus estimate for 'Remaining performance obligation (RPO) - Current' stands at $33.46 billion. The estimate is in contrast to the year-ago figure of $29.40 billion.
